description: Complete the SQL statements to create and manage a customer table with proper Delta Lake syntax.
expectedOutput:
When completed correctly, this code will:
1. Create a 'customers' table with STRING IDs, INT purchase counts, stored as DELTA format
2. Insert 2 customer records (Alice with 5 purchases, Bob with 0)
3. Increment Alice's purchase count from 5 to 6 using a column expression
4. Filter to show only customers with purchases > 3, sorted newest first
codeTemplate:
-- Create a customer table with Delta Lake
CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id __BLANK_0__,
    name STRING,
    email STRING,
    signup_date DATE,
    total_purchases __BLANK_1__
) USING __BLANK_2__
LOCATION '__BLANK_3__';

-- Insert customer records
INSERT INTO customers VALUES
  ('C001', 'Alice Johnson', 'alice@example.com', '2024-01-10', 5),
  ('C002', 'Bob Smith', 'bob@example.com', '2024-01-11', 0);

-- Update purchase count
UPDATE customers
SET total_purchases = __BLANK_4__
WHERE customer_id = 'C001';

-- Query with filtering
SELECT * FROM customers
WHERE total_purchases __BLANK_5__ 3
ORDER BY signup_date __BLANK_6__;
hints: Delta Lake tables use 'USING DELTA' in CREATE TABLE syntax
STRING is the preferred type for IDs in Databricks (not VARCHAR)
INT is sufficient for counting purchases (no decimals needed)
Unity Catalog Volumes are the recommended storage location for managed Delta tables (not /mnt/)
UPDATE can reference the existing column value (e.g., column + 1) to increment without hardcoding
Use '>' to filter rows where the column exceeds a threshold
learnings: STRING is preferred over VARCHAR for IDs in Databricks
USING DELTA specifies the Delta Lake format for ACID transactions
INT is sufficient for count columns (no decimals needed)
Unity Catalog Volumes (not /mnt/ mount points) are the modern storage location for Delta tables
Column expressions (column + 1) reference existing values in UPDATE — essential for incremental logic
